title: Design-system page-layout manifest
description:
Contract for the layout manifest a design system publishes about its own page layouts (e.g. `packages/layout/layouts.json`). The agentic-design engine finds it via the adapter's `layoutManifest` and generates a layout decision table into the consuming repo, so the 'which layout should this page use?' question is answered from the DS's source of truth instead of being hand-copied into every repo's ds.config.json.

WHO OWNS THIS FILE: the design system, versioned and reviewed in the same PR that adds a layout. The DS is expected to enforce manifest/source parity itself (e.g. a unit test asserting every exported `*Template` has an entry). The engine additionally reports exports it finds with no manifest entry as `unclassified` — it never guesses their kind.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this contract, for editor completion.

package.description: The npm package the layouts are exported from, e.g. "@fiscozen/layout". Used as the default `import` for every entry and cross-referenced against the component inventory to detect entries that are in source but not yet in the published version.

indexPath.description: Optional. Path (relative to the manifest's own directory) of the barrel whose exports are the authoritative layout list, e.g. "src/index.ts". The engine diffs it against `layouts[]` to surface manifest drift. Defaults to "src/index.ts".

exportPattern.description: Optional ERE matched against the barrel's export names to decide which are page layouts, e.g. "Template$". Names matching the pattern but absent from `layouts[]` are reported as drift. Defaults to "Template$". Set it to something the DS's own naming supports; a DS whose layouts have no common suffix should list them in `layouts[]` and set this to a pattern matching exactly those (or accept the drift report being advisory).

layouts.description: One entry per layout, in the order a developer should consider them (most common first). Regions and grid primitives are listed too, so the engine can tell an agent NOT to reach for them directly.

name.description: Exported component name, e.g. "FzAppTemplate". Must match the barrel export exactly.

kind.description:
What role the layout plays — the single most important field, because it decides how the layout may be used:

- `shell`: a top-level page shell that owns the viewport height. Exactly one per page, at the router-view level.
- `page-content`: renders INSIDE a shell's content slot. Never top-level. Usually paired with a shell (see `nestWithin`).
- `bounded`: fills the height of its parent and needs a bounded-height ancestor. Collapses to zero height if that contract isn't met — the riskiest kind, so `nestWithin` should list only VERIFIED hosts.
- `region`: an internal region wrapper the layouts themselves compose. NOT for app code; the engine blocks direct use in consuming repos.
- `grid`: a low-level grid/arrangement primitive for in-page composition, not a page layout.

import.description: Import specifier, if it differs from `package` (e.g. a subpath export).

surfaces.description: Product surfaces this layout is intended for, drawn from the adapter's `surfaces` (e.g. ["FO"], ["BO"], ["FO", "BO"]). Drives the surface passed to the design-principles review, whose severity and tone depend on it. Omit when surface-neutral.

since.description: Package version the layout first shipped in, e.g. "1.2.0". The engine compares it against the version in the component inventory and flags entries whose `since` is ahead of the published version as NOT YET AVAILABLE — the failure mode where an agent installs the current release and the import doesn't resolve.

whenToUse.description: One or two sentences a non-technical designer would recognise: the page shape this layout is for. This is the text the layout decision is actually made from, so describe the SHAPE ("list page: filter rail beside a table"), not the implementation.

notWhenToUse.description: Optional but strongly recommended for any layout that is easily confused with another: what this is NOT for, naming the alternative. This is where near-miss mistakes get prevented (e.g. a three-column page template vs. a grid primitive's three-column variant).

slots.description: Named slots, in render order, with the default slot written as "default". Kept in sync with the component's slot type by the DS's own parity test.

keyProps.description: Props worth surfacing at plan time (not the exhaustive list — the component source stays authoritative for signatures).

heightContract.description:
How the layout establishes its height — the contract most often violated when layouts are nested:

- `owns-viewport`: owns a full-height root (e.g. `min-h-dvh`); does not depend on app-global height CSS.
- `document-scroll`: grows with its content and lets the document scroll; the host owns the scroll container and device safe-area.
- `fills-parent`: fills its parent's height and scrolls its regions internally; REQUIRES a bounded-height ancestor.

nestWithin.description: For `page-content` and `bounded` layouts: the hosts this layout is VERIFIED to work inside — ideally backed by a composition test in the DS, not inferred from prose. Height contracts interact in non-obvious ways (a `fills-parent` layout inside a `min-height`-based shell is not self-evidently bounded), so an unverified pair belongs in `composeOnly.gaps` or `notWhenToUse`, not here.

whenNested.description: What a consumer must change when this layout is nested inside a host — the props that avoid duplicate landmarks and ambiguous accessible names.

props.description: Prop → required value when nested, e.g. { "mainAs": "div" } to avoid a second `main` landmark inside a shell that already owns one.

note.description: Anything else the consumer must do, e.g. set an accessible name when the host contributes its own complementary landmark.

composeOnly.description: Whether this layout's documented capabilities are all reachable through its public API under a `compose-only` styling policy — i.e. without a fall-through `class` or `style` on the layout root. A layout whose only route to a documented capability is a class/inline style is not usable as documented in a compose-only repo, and the engine warns about it at PLAN time rather than letting the developer discover it when a write is blocked.

safe.description: true when every documented capability is reachable via props/slots/tokens alone.

gaps.description: One line per capability that currently requires a class/style, ideally naming the tracking ticket. Shown to the agent before it commits to this layout.

docs.description: Optional link or repo-relative path to fuller documentation (README section, RFC, ADR).
